newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares tumble, unnerved by Ergobank plunge.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares tumble, unnerved by Ergobank plunge.

text.p: The Athens bourse came under selling pressure on Thursday as jitters from Ergobank's 5.29 percent plunge spread into the market leading the benchmark index 1.69 percent lower.

"There was a significant fall today led by Ergo Bank because of a lack of consensus on its planned 27.3 billion drachma rights issue. This affected other bank shares to a lesser extent but sparked selling pressure," said broker George Kounadis at Alki Brokerage.
Ergo Bank has rescheduled a shareholders meeting for December 17 after a proposal by one of its shareholders, Lazaros Efremoglou, who opposed the rights issue.
"Ergo Bank's fall unnerved the market as banks had led the recovery after the Delta Securities scandal causing players to reassess the market's trend and question the recent rebound," he said.
It was the sixth normal session since a settlement scandal halted trading for almost four days.

Kounadis expected the benchmark index to stabilise around 900 points -- a psychologically significant support level. December, historically a good month for equities, could see stocks at higher levels, he said.
On Monday brokers association president resolved a disagreement over a draft bill on the exchange after meeting with National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou.
The Athens general share index was closed down 1.36 percent or 12.45 points lower at 900.65, above the session's 896.95 low, from Wednesday's 913.10 close after opening at 911.99.
Turnover was 5.26 billion drachmas on volume of 1.95 million shares.
